prompt:
Pixel art emblem of the zodiac sign GEMINI: two identical heads in profile facing each other, nose to nose, mirror images, one magenta and one sky blue, their long hair sweeping back and up into two wing-like curls; the gap between the two faces forms the shape of a tall vase or flame. One star above each head.

Layout, the same as the other emblems in this set: a thin-lined regular hexagon frame (all six sides equal, point at the top), large, almost touching the edges of the square image. The emblem sits in the middle and fills most of the hexagon, overlapping its outline slightly. Behind the hexagon, mirrored ribbons of wind spiral outward past the frame on both sides, like the sunburst behind a sun emblem.

This is a SYMBOL, not a character: a timeless emblem like a heraldic crest, a carved totem or a stained-glass roundel. Front-facing, perfectly symmetrical left to right, still and dignified, so that anyone born under the sign can see themselves in it. No cartoon expression, no mascot, no cuteness, no story. The faces are calm, simple and neutral, eyes open, lips closed. The sign's nature shows only through form: perfect mirror symmetry, light airy curves, two halves of one whole: duality, quickness, exchange.

Style: bold simplified geometric shapes with thick dark outlines between them, 16-bit console pixel art, hard square pixels, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no gradients, no dithering. Drawn on a 96 x 96 pixel grid, shown enlarged so each pixel is a clear square. The whole image has a flat solid BLACK background, edge to edge.

Palette: exactly four flat colours plus black: cream, magenta, yellow, sky blue. At most two flat shades of each, nothing else.

Square image, no text, no letters, no watermark, no signature.
